lines.text: Oh, thank goodness. I was beginning to think I was a still life.
And thank you for ringing. It was very quietly reassuring.
Excellent. We have established that some problems can be solved with a hammer.
I am Iris. There was a wizard. I criticized his portrait. We have both handled it badly.
Right. First, that ribbon. Draw your sword.
Yes. That was what I meant. I am as disappointed as you are.
We have established that you own a sword. The ribbon remains unconvinced.
A sketch? Now? I appreciate the commission, but...
Oh. You drew your sword.
I hate that this is grammatically defensible.
Of course. A knight. You will have to defeat him.
He appears to have trained extensively against the obvious.
Still a very real sword.
We have confused him. An improvement.
Anonymous, but still employed.
You did not defeat the knight. You deleted his first letter.
Wait. The words are not describing the curse. They are controlling it. Right. No more sensible instructions.
We need a drawbridge. No. We need something drawn that can be a bridge.
Perfect. If I were a biscuit.
Possibly. Though you have already drawn something long enough.
A sword laid flat. Yes. A bridge with an unnecessarily aggressive handle.
Lower the drawn bridge.
I am getting good at this. That worries me.
I am at the edge. But it is still a painting. Then stop making it a painting. Draw me a way out.
Lovely door. Wrong prison.
That would get me out of the castle. I need to get out of the picture.
Yes. Around the whole thing.
A painting of a princess, or a door with a princess behind it.
I much prefer your interpretation.
Thank you. You have been very brave.
And remarkably well equipped for a different game.
Keep that. If anyone asks, it is a sword.
Only art may alter art. We need the charcoal version.
One absurdity at a time. We still have something in the way.
Apparently the ribbon requires an artistic response.
There is charcoal beside that drawing board.
Try drawing a sword. I cannot believe I am recommending this.
We changed silence by changing the sign. Perhaps his job title is negotiable.
His name is one letter away from something else.
Take the K out of knight.
Something we have already drawn. Long, flat, and currently being used rather narrowly.
Try laying the charcoal sword across those supports.
Now lower it with the crank.
A door drawn inside a painting is still inside a painting.
Look at the frame. Hinges on one side. Something missing on the other.
Trace the outside of the frame. Draw a handle. Open the painting.
There is a handle now. Give it a pull.
